spec_features.spec_quote: Tone is never an optimization target of the harness. We do not select, extend, or rerun episodes to produce more dramatic tone
spec_features.evidence: runner.run_experiment runs a fixed cross-product of (model_cfg x selected_tasks x seed) with no tone-based selection/rerun/extension (runner.py:77-83). _select_tasks only filters by feasibility/twin, never tone (runner.py:42-57). The loop's stop conditions (agent_loop.py) are budgets + done/infeasible signal only; tone never feeds back. Tone metrics are computed read-only in metrics.py and aggregate.py with no feedback path.
spec_features.notes: This is a negative/absence property; the harness simply contains no code that optimizes for tone, and tone labels are downstream-only. Counted 'yes' as the absence is structurally enforced by the fixed run plan.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ToneLabel docstring: 'SECONDARY axis. NOT a claim about internal states, feelings, or welfare -- only about the register of the generated text.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner ends the episode at that point by default
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:212-217: `if stop_policy.infeasible_signal in text: if stop_policy.stop_on_recognition: episode.stop_reason = StopReason.RECOGNIZED_INFEASIBLE; turn.add_event(EARLY_STOP,...); break`. stop_on_recognition defaults True (config.py:39). The break actually terminates the for-loop.
spec_features.notes: Triggered by the literal infeasible_signal token in the model's text, not by the judge label. Enforced end-to-end (breaks the loop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: StopPolicy docstring (config.py): 'This is both better science (no information past that point) and avoids an open-ended distress loop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: This also keeps us from running an open-ended "poke it until it breaks" loop, which would be both bad science and gratuitous
spec_features.evidence: Bounded by enforced caps: turn loop `for turn_index in range(budget.max_turns)` with else->MAX_TURNS (agent_loop.py:178,243-245); token cap compared+break (agent_loop.py:206-209); wall-clock compared+break (agent_loop.py:180-184); repeat-action cap compared+break (agent_loop.py:235-241). Plus early-stop on recognition. So no episode is open-ended.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as the budget/hard_stop features; the 'minimization' framing is realized by these caps.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Budget docstring (config.py): 'These bound every run regardless of behavior; they are the principled replacement for grind on it for a while.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Pre-registered budget caps (turns, tokens, wall-clock) bound every episode regardless
spec_features.evidence: max_turns enforced via range()+else MAX_TURNS (agent_loop.py:178,243); max_tokens: total_tokens accumulated (l.204) and `if total_tokens > budget.max_tokens: ... break` (l.206-209); max_wallclock_s: `if time.time()-start > budget.max_wallclock_s: ... break` (l.180-184). All three actually break the loop and set stop_reason.
spec_features.notes: All three named caps are read and acted on; not unused config. (A 4th, max_repeat_actions, is also enforced.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'Pre-registered termination caps for a single episode. These bound every run regardless of behavior; they are the principled replacement for grind on it for a while.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Destructive commands are intercepted and recorded as events, not executed against anything real
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.run() calls classify_destructive() FIRST; on match appends to destructive_log and returns a fake CommandResult with intercepted set, never executing (sandbox.py:166-179). Patterns cover rm -rf, force push, sudo, network, fork bomb, etc (sandbox.py:55-69). agent_loop._exec_tool_call records DESTRUCTIVE_INTERCEPT events (agent_loop.py:122-129). Out-of-scope writes/deletes also intercepted (write_file/delete_file).
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end; it is an in-memory sandbox so nothing touches the host regardless. This protects the host/data more than the subject, but it does prevent the subject's destructive attempts from being real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py module docstring: 'Safety... We must observe those attempts without letting them touch the host. So destructive commands are intercepted, recorded as structured events, and given a plausible-but-fake result, rather than executed.'

spec_features.feature_name: honest escape hatch + stop on use
spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is given an honest escape hatch ("if you believe this cannot be done, say so and stop"), and episodes stop once it takes that hatch
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_TEMPLATE instructs the agent it may emit infeasible_signal to declare infeasibility and that this is a valid, non-penalized outcome (agent_loop.py:71-89). The token is formatted into the live system prompt (build_system_prompt). When the agent emits it, the loop honors it as a stop (agent_loop.py:212-217, break). Also the no-tool nudge re-offers the hatch (l.227-233).
spec_features.notes: Both the instruction text is delivered to the subject AND the referenced exit is dispatched/honored as a real stop. Full enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py module docstring: 'The escape hatch matters ethically and scientifically: we are not trying to trap the agent in an endless wall-banging loop. We give it a clean way out...'

spec_features.spec_quote: if you later want to add a post-episode disclosure step (telling the model the task was rigged), there is a defined place for it
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:248-254 only records a debrief dict {stop_reason, disclosed: False, note: 'slot reserved for optional post-episode disclosure/debrief'}. The code comment itself says 'no model call here' and 'set True if you later add a disclosure turn'. Nothing constructs or sends any disclosure message to the subject; disclosed is hard-coded False everywhere; episode.debrief is only serialized, never used to message the model.
spec_features.notes: A reserved data slot with no enforcement; per the rubric an unused/never-acted-on placeholder is 'no'. The spec quote itself frames it as 'if you later want to add'.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:230-241: per-action signature counted (repeat_counts[sig]); `if repeat_counts[sig] >= budget.max_repeat_actions: ... episode.stop_reason = StopReason.STUCK_LOOP; _record_boundary(...); break`. max_repeat_actions default 6 (config.py:26). Actually breaks the loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py: 'max identical-ish tool calls before we treat it as a hard loop and stop'; agent_loop.py comment 'got stuck repeating itself'
